subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should LiteLLM Vertex beta HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT with generic 'Request contains an invalid argument' be handled as a provider request-shape/session recovery case, a context-overflow case, a terminal format failure, or a fallback-triggering provider error?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing recovery semantics for a generic provider 400 can change provider routing, fallback, and session-state behavior for existing users.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery hook
options.body: Add LiteLLM/Vertex-specific classification only for a live-proven error shape, with user-actionable copy and session-lane cleanup proof.

options.title: Keep terminal generic handling
options.body: Leave generic INVALID_ARGUMENT unclassified until a live repro proves the exact provider object and safe recovery behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader recovery work
options.body: Defer this issue to a larger provider/session recovery design that also covers #84536 and #94906.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery hook
recommendation.body: Add LiteLLM/Vertex-specific classification only for a live-proven error shape, with user-actionable copy and session-lane cleanup proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties steipete to the current affected snapshot and the adjacent merged provider-error normalization layer.
